issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Proposition asym-dim-ge applies a local limit theorem with an explicit remainder to sums of independent uniform variables. In the GE-PI case the block distributions are Gaussian-binomial (Takács) laws with N_j and l both bounded. No argument is given that the Petrov-type expansion, with its O(1/N^2) remainder and the Hermite correction, holds for them. The paper itself says it could not prove the single-block case (Conjecture asym-dim-gepi-1block), whose O(N^{-5/2}) remainder is the same kind of claim. Yet the multi-block statement, which contains that case when N_b=1, is stated as a proved proposition with a one-line proof by analogy. The block cumulants are quoted without derivation.

failure_location.quote: The proof is similar to the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:asym-dim-ge}, using the variance given in~\cite[(43)]{takacs1986asymptotic}, and the fourth-order cumulants

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove the local expansion with remainder for sums of independent Gaussian-binomial blocks, or downgrade the statement to a conjecture or to an o(.) result that follows from the cited limit.
issues.overall_effect: The O(Nb^{-5/2}) error term in dimpi-est is unsupported. The numerically used estimate for N=80 and the claim that GE-PI dimensions follow the same asymptotics rest on an unproved statement.
issues.title: Proof of the general-l GE-PI asymptotic dimension is only asserted by analogy
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial argument (a local limit theorem for non-identical block laws) or a weakening of the remainder is needed, and the rest of the paper is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Numerical simulations are provided to show that the proposed method scales linearly instead of exponentially for existing methods in the literature.

issues.failure_explanation: The derived bound is the product of the number of basis functions dim, the number of classes and the row-sparsity factor 2Σl+1. It is linear in a product of two growing quantities, not in the number of basis functions. The classes are themselves counted separately from the basis functions. The back-substitution bound is also only an upper bound, not a proved scaling law. The exponential behaviour of other packages is inferred from a few log-log plots truncated at 10^6 ms, with no complexity analysis of those codes. The paper's own Figure 4 and the text describe polynomial, not linear, scaling.

failure_location.quote: Indeed, our method scales almost linearly with respect to the number of basis functions, largely outperforming existing packages in the literature, which typically scale exponentially with respect to the number of basis functions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim as an upper bound of order (dim+1)(2Σl+1)·(number of classes), or as polynomial in classes and dimension, and describe the comparison with other packages as empirical.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claims in the abstract and conclusion (linear instead of exponential scaling) are not established by the analysis or experiments.
issues.title: Linear-scaling and exponential-scaling claims exceed what the cost bound and benchmarks establish
issues.why_classification: Only the wording of the scaling claims needs correcting, since the method and the stated cost bound remain valid.
